rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening recalls the time Moses declared that he would keep traveling until reaching the meeting place of the two seas.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإذا ﴾ واذكر إذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attendant is Joshua son of Nun; he is called Moses’ young companion because he served and followed him and learned from him.
rows.anchor: هو يوشع بن نون وانما قيل فتاه لأنه كان يخدمه ويتبعه ويأخذ منه العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā abraḥ means I continue; its predicate, travel, is omitted because the journey is underway and the stated destination supplies the sense.
rows.anchor: لا أزال وقد حذف الخبر لدلالة الحال والكلام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting place is where Moses was promised he would meet al-Khidr, at the junction of the Persian and Roman seas.
rows.anchor: وهو المكان الذي وعد فيه موسى لقاء الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr was named because greenery appears around him wherever he arrives.
rows.anchor: وسمى خضرا لأنه أينما يصل يخضر ما حوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huquban means a long stretch of time; one report specifies eighty years.
rows.anchor: أو أسير زمانا طويلا قيل ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An extended report says Moses, after Israel settled in Egypt following Pharaoh’s people’s destruction, asked God who was most beloved, most just, and most learned; God praised remembrance, just judgment, and seeking knowledge, then identified al-Khidr as more learned.
rows.anchor: روى أنه لما ظهر موسى عليه السلام على مصر مع بني اسرائيل واستقروا بها بعد هلاك القبط سأل ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report locates al-Khidr at the seashore by a rock and tells Moses to carry a fish in a basket; wherever it is lost is the meeting place, so Moses instructs Joshua to alert him.
rows.anchor: قال على الساحل عند الصخرة قال يا رب كيف لي به قال تأخذ حوتا في مكتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same report Moses sleeps, the fish leaps into the sea, and Joshua tells him at the meal; they return to the rock, find a man under a covering, and al-Khidr says each has knowledge the other lacks.
rows.anchor: قرقد موسى فاضطرب الحوت ووقع في البحر فلما جاء وقت الغداء طلب موسى الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The place where the two seas meet is the confluence of the two waters.
rows.anchor: مجمع البحرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only one of the two forgot the fish, namely Joshua, who was in charge of their provisions; this explains the plural wording as in saying that they forgot their food.
rows.anchor: أي نسي أحدهما وهو يوشع لأنه كان صاحب الزاد دليله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the salted fish revived from the water’s life-giving freshness after they slept overnight beside its spring, then fell into the water.
rows.anchor: قيل كان الحوت سمكة مملوحة فنزلا ليلة على شاطيء عين الحياة ونام موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish made a passage from land into the sea.
rows.anchor: أي اتخذ طريقا له من البر إلى البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saraban is an accusative verbal noun: the fish entered the sea and concealed itself there.
rows.anchor: نصب على المصدر أي سرب فيه سربا يعني دخل فيه واستتر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had passed the meeting place and then stopped after traveling as long as God willed.
rows.anchor: مجمع البحرين ثم نزلا وقد سارا ما شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says they have become tired on this journey; he had not been tired or hungry before then.
rows.anchor: تعبا ولم يتعب ولا جاع قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rock was the appointed meeting place.
rows.anchor: هي موضع الموعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joshua first says he forgot the fish and then offers his excuse.
rows.anchor: بدل من الهاء في أنسانية أي وما أنساني ذكره إلا الشيطان

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads the attached pronoun in ansānīhi with a ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وبضم الهاء حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan caused the forgetting by casting distracting thoughts into the heart.
rows.anchor: بالقاء الخواطر في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an adhkurahu replaces the pronoun in ansānīhi, specifying that Satan made him forget to mention the fish.
rows.anchor: بدل من الهاء في أنسانية أي وما أنساني ذكره إلا الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The marvel was that the fish’s trace remained along the route it took.
rows.anchor: وهو أن أثره بقي إلى حيث سار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabghi means seek; the fish’s departure signaled that they had found the place where they would meet al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال ذلك ما كنا نبغ ﴾ نطلب

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The Meccan reading retains the final yāʾ in nabghi; Abū ʿAmr, ʿAlī, and Madani agree when connecting, while the other form follows the written codex without yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالياء مكي وافقه أبو عمرو وعلى ومدني في الوصل وبغير ياء فيهما اتباعا لخط المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went back along the road by which they had come, following their own tracks.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فارتدا على آثارهما ﴾ فرجعا في الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣan means following tracks, and al-Zajjāj glosses al-qaṣaṣ as following a trace.
rows.anchor: يقصان قصصا أي يتبعان آثارهما اتباعا قال الزجاج القصص اتباع الاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is al-Khidr, whom Moses found either asleep beneath a covering or seated in the sea.
rows.anchor: أي الخضر راقدا تحت ثوب أو جالسا في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy given from God is variously explained as revelation and prophethood, knowledge, or long life.
rows.anchor: هي الوحي والنبوة أو العلم أو طول الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge taught directly by God refers to reports of unseen matters.
rows.anchor: يعني الاخبار بالغيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls ladunnī knowledge that a servant receives through inspiration.
rows.anchor: وقيل العلم اللدني ما حصل للعبد بطريق الالهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks to follow al-Khidr and learn knowledge that guides him rightly in his religion.
rows.anchor: أي علما ذا رشد به في ديني

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the variant rushd; both forms are Arabic dialects, like the two forms of bukhl.
rows.anchor: رشدا أبو عمر وهما لغتان كالبخل والبخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one should stop seeking knowledge even after reaching the limit of learning, and one should be humble before someone more learned.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه لا ينبغي لأحد أن يترك طلب العلم وان كان قد بلغ نهايته

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads the yāʾ in maʿiya with fatḥa, as he does in the other occurrences later in the surah.
rows.anchor: وبفتح الياء حفص وكذا ما بعده في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patience al-Khidr doubts is Moses’ ability to refrain from objecting and asking questions.
rows.anchor: أي عن الانكار والسؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khubran specifies and emphatically clarifies the denied ability to be patient with al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: تمييز نفي استطاعة الصبر معه على وجه التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr explains that he will undertake acts outwardly reprehensible; even a righteous man cannot contain his distress at seeing them, much less a prophet.
rows.anchor: تولى أمورا هي في ظاهرها مناكير والرجل الصالح لا يتمالك أن يجزع إذا رأى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises to be among those who patiently refrain from objection and disagreement.
rows.anchor: من الصابرين عن الانكار والاعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-lā aʿṣī is accusative, coordinated with ṣābiran, and means Moses will not disobey; syntactically it also coordinates with sat ajidunī.
rows.anchor: في محل النصب عطف على صابرا أي ستجدني صابرا وغير عاص وهو عطف على ستجدني

rows.speaker: مدني
rows.claim: Madani and Shami read with a fatḥa on the lām and a doubled nūn; the others read a still lām and light nūn, and all retain the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: بفتح اللام وتشديد النون مدني وشامي وبسكون اللام وتخفيف النون غيرهما والياء ثابتة فيهما اجماعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A condition of following is that the student who sees an apparently sound act whose rationale is hidden should not question or challenge the teacher until the teacher explains it.
rows.anchor: فمن شرط اتباعك لي انك إذا رأيت مني شيئا وقد علمت انه صحيح إلا أنه خفي عليك وجه صحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waiting for the teacher to open the explanation is proper etiquette for a student with a teacher and a follower with a leader.
rows.anchor: حتى أكون أنا الفاتح عليك وهذا من أدب المتعلم مع العالم والمتبوع مع التابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They searched along the shore for a boat; its owners suspected them of theft, but the boat’s master recognized prophetic faces and carried them without fare.
rows.anchor: فانطلقا على ساحل البحر يطلبان السفينة فلما ركباها قال أهلها هما من اللصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they reached open water, al-Khidr took an axe and pulled out two planks on the water-facing side; Moses plugged the hole with his clothes.
rows.anchor: فلما لججوا أخذ الخضر الفأس فخرق السفينة بأن قلع لوحين من ألواحها مما يلي الماء

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read the verb in the intransitive sense, to sink or drown.
rows.anchor: ليغرق حمزة وعلى من غرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran means a grave, immense matter, from the expression for when a matter becomes great.
rows.anchor: أتيت شيئا عظيما من أمر الأمر إذا عظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr repeats his warning; Moses had seen that water did not enter through the hole and had not fled the boat.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى موسى أن الخرق لا يدخله الماء ولم يفر من السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses may mean that he forgot al-Khidr’s warning, something he forgot, or his own forgetfulness; on this reading, forgetfulness is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: بالذي نسيته أو بشيء نسيته أو بنسياني أراد أنه نسي وصيته ولا مؤاخذة على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nasiya means leave or neglect: Moses asks not to be taken to task for having neglected the warning the first time.
rows.anchor: أو أراد بالنسيان الترك أي لا تؤاخذني بما تركت من وصيتك أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahaqa means to cover; Moses asks not to be overwhelmed with difficulty in following al-Khidr, but for him to make the following easy by overlooking and not debating.
rows.anchor: رهقه إذا غشيه وأرهقه اياه أي ولا تغشني عسرا من أمري وهو اتباعه إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says al-Khidr struck the boy’s head against a wall; another says he laid him down and slaughtered him with a knife.
rows.anchor: قيل ضرب برأسه الحائط وقيل اضجعه ثم ذبحه بالسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship clause lacks fa because its damage is the result of boarding, whereas the killing takes fa because it is grouped inside the conditional sequence and follows meeting the boy immediately.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال فقتله بالفاء وقال خرقها بغير فاء لأن خرقها جعل جزاء للشرط وجعل قتله من جملة الشرط

rows.speaker: حجازي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Hijazi readers and Abū ʿAmr use the variant zakiyya for the boy described as pure.
rows.anchor: ﴿ زكية ﴾ زاكية حجازي وأبو عمرو وهي الطاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy is called pure either because Moses had not seen him sin or because he was too young to have reached the age of sin.
rows.anchor: أما لأنها طاهرة عنده لأنه لم يرها قد اذنبت أو لأنها صغيرة لم تبلغ الحنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying without a life in return, Moses means the boy had killed no one and was not liable to retaliation.
rows.anchor: أي لم تقتل نفسا فيقتص منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Najda the Haruri wrote asking how the killing was permitted despite the Prophet’s prohibition on killing children; Ibn Abbas replied that only someone who knew the child’s condition as Moses’ knower did could do it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما ان نجدة الحروري كتب اليه كيف جاز قتله وقد نهى رسول الله

rows.speaker: مدني وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Madani and Abu Bakr read nukran with a ḍamma on the kāf wherever the word occurs; it means objectionable.
rows.anchor: وبضم الكاف حيث كان مدني وابو بكر وهو المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One comparison says nukr is less than imr because killing one person is less than drowning the boat’s people.
rows.anchor: وقيل النكر أقل من الأمر لأن قتل نفس واحدة أهون من إغراق أهل السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another comparison says this was more reprehensible than the first act because a hole can be repaired, while a killing cannot be undone.
rows.anchor: أو معناه جئت شيئا أنكر من الأول لأن الخرق يمكن تداركه بالسد ولا يمكن تدارك القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr adds laka, for you, because the second act involved greater reprehensibility.
rows.anchor: زاد ذلك هنا لان النكر فيه أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿdahā can mean after this occasion or after this question.
rows.anchor: بعد هذه الكرة أو المسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he has cleared al-Khidr of blame in the matter of their separation.
rows.anchor: أعذرت فيما بيني وبينك في الفراق

rows.speaker: مدني وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Madani and Abu Bakr read ladunni with a light nūn.
rows.anchor: بتخفيف النون مدني وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town is identified as Antioch or al-Abullah; al-Abullah is described as the land farthest from the sky.
rows.anchor: هي انطاكية أو الأبلة وهي أبعد أرض الله من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaṭʿamā means they asked the townspeople to host them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ استطعما أهلها ﴾ استضافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍayyafahu means to lodge someone and make him a guest.
rows.anchor: ضيفه أنزله وجعله ضيفه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet called the townspeople a miserly community; another report says the worst villages are those that withhold hospitality.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام كانوا أهل قرية لئاما وقيل شر القرى التي تبخل بالقرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall in the town was one hundred cubits tall.
rows.anchor: ﴿ جدارا ﴾ طوله مائة ذراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall’s wanting to collapse means it was close to falling; desire and resolve are figuratively used for nearing an event.
rows.anchor: يكاد يسقط استعيرت الارادة للمداناة والمشارقة كما استعير الهم العزم لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr may have raised the wall with his hand, rubbed it until it stood, or dismantled and rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: بيده أو مسحه بيده فقام واستوى أو نقضه وبناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were desperate and hungry, had reached a person’s last resort of asking, and found no one to help; seeing this deprivation prompted Moses to mention a wage to relieve their need.
rows.anchor: كانت الحال حال اضطرار وافتقار إلى المطعم وقد لزتهما الحاجة إلى آخر كسب المرء وهو المسألة

rows.speaker: بصري
rows.claim: Basrans read the verb for taking wages with a light tāʾ, a kasra on khāʾ, and assimilation of dhāl.
rows.anchor: لتخذت بتخفيف التاء وكسر الخاء وادغام الذال بصرى

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The Meccan reading keeps dhāl unassimilated in the light-tāʾ form.
rows.anchor: وباظهارها مكي

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs doubles tāʾ, opens khāʾ, and pronounces dhāl distinctly.
rows.anchor: وبتشديد التاء وفتح الخاء واظهار الذال حفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers double tāʾ, open khāʾ, and assimilate dhāl into tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبتشديد التاء وفتح الخاء وادغام الذال في التاء غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in takhadha is a root consonant, as in tabaʿa; ittakhadha is derived from it on the iftiʿāl pattern, and is unrelated to akhdh, taking.
rows.anchor: والتاء في تخذ أصل كما في تبع واتخذا افتعل منه كاتبع من تبع وليس من الأخذ في شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third question is what Moses means by this separation: his objection has caused the two companions to part.
rows.anchor: هذا اشارة إلى السؤال الثالت أي هذا الاعتراض سبب الفراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying wording is firaqu bayni wa-baynika; a reading has that form, with the verbal noun annexed to an adverb as it can be annexed to an object.
rows.anchor: والاصل هذا فراق بيني وبينك وقد قرئ به فاضيف المصدر إلى الظرف كما يضاف إلى المفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boat belonged to poor people who earned their living at sea.
rows.anchor: فكانت لمساكين يعملون في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says ten brothers owned it: five were disabled and five worked at sea.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت لعشرة أخوة خمسة منهم زمنى وخمسة يعملون في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr intended to make the boat defective.
rows.anchor: أجعلها ذات عيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waraʾahum can mean ahead of them or behind them; their return route passed the king, and God had informed al-Khidr though the boat owners did not know.
rows.anchor: أمامهم أو خلفهم وكان طريقهم في رجوعهم عليه وما كان عندهم خبرة أعلم الله به الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king was Julandi and seized every sound, undamaged boat by force, leaving defective ones alone.
rows.anchor: أي يأخذ كل سفينة صالحة لا عيب فيها غصبا وان كانت معيبة تركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaṣban is either an absolute verbal noun or an object of reason.
rows.anchor: وان كانت معيبة تركها وهو مصدر أو مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although damaging the boat was caused by fear of seizure and would naturally follow that cause, the act is mentioned first for emphasis.
rows.anchor: فكان حقه أن يتأخر عن السبب قلت المراد به التأخير وانما قدم للعناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy was named al-Husayn.
rows.anchor: وكان اسمه الحسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr feared the boy would oppress his believing parents, repay their care with disobedience and mistreatment, bring them trouble, or lead them astray until they renounced faith.
rows.anchor: فخفنا أن يغشى الوالدين المؤمنين طغيانا عليهما وكفرا لنعمتهما بعقوقه وسوء صنيعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is al-Khidr’s speech; he feared the child’s future because God informed him of the boy’s condition and disclosed the matter’s secret.
rows.anchor: وهو من كلام الخضر وإنما خشي الخضر منه ذلك لانه تعالى اعلمه بحاله واطلعه على سر أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the words are God’s speech, fakhashīnā means We knew that, if the boy lived, he would cause his parents’ disbelief.
rows.anchor: فمعنى فخشينا فعلمنا ان عاش ان يصير سببا لكفر والديه

rows.speaker: مدني وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Madani and Abu Amr read yubaddiluhumā rabbuhumā, with their Lord as the one who replaces the child for the parents.
rows.anchor: يبدلهما ربهما مدني وابو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakātan means purity and freedom from sins.
rows.anchor: طهارة ونقاء من الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥman means affection and compassion; the two forms are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: رحما وعطفا وزكاة وحرما تمييز

rows.speaker: شامي
rows.claim: The Shami reading uses the variant rahman for compassion.
rows.anchor: رحما شامي وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a girl was born to the parents, married a prophet, and gave birth to a prophet.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأقرب رحما ﴾ رحما وعطفا وزكاة وحرما تمييز روى أنه ولدت لهما جارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says their Lord replaced him with a believing son like them, characterized by compassion.
rows.anchor: أو أبدلهما ابنا مؤمنا مثلهما رحما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two orphan boys were named Asram and Sarim, and the city was the same town mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين ﴾ اصرم وصريم ﴿ يتيمين في المدينة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasure may have been a gold tablet with maxims about belief in destiny, provision, death, judgment, and the world’s instability; the author calls this interpretation the clearest.
rows.anchor: أي لوح من ذهب مكتوب فيه عجبت لمن يؤمن بالقدر كيف يحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the treasure was buried gold and silver or written pages containing knowledge.
rows.anchor: أو مال مدفون من ذهب وفضة أو صحف فيها علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the explanation that the treasure was a gold tablet bearing wisdom sayings.
rows.anchor: والأول أظهر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says treasure was permitted to earlier communities but prohibited for this community, while spoils were prohibited to them and permitted to Muslims.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة احل الكنز لمن قبلنا وحرم علينا وحرمت الغنيمة عليهم وأحلت لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say their father was their seventh-generation grandfather.
rows.anchor: قيل جدهما السابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn Ali was told that God protected the boys because of their father’s righteousness; he replied that his own father and grandfather were better.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسين بن علي رضي الله عنهما انه قال لبعض الخوارج في كلام جرى بينهما بم حفظ الله الغلامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father’s righteousness is described as the quality of someone who accompanies al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: ممن يصحبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd refers to reaching puberty.
rows.anchor: أي الحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmatan can be an object of reason or a verbal noun whose sense is that God had mercy on them.
rows.anchor: مفعول له أو مصدر منصوب بارادة ربك لأنه في معنى رحمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What al-Khidr did refers to what Moses saw; he acted by God’s command rather than by his own judgment, and the pronoun may refer to all three acts or just the wall.
rows.anchor: عن اجتهادي وانما فعلته بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding interpretation concerns the three answers and the explanation of what Moses could not patiently bear; the final tāʾ is omitted for ease.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ أي الاجوبة الثلاثة ﴿ تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا ﴾ حذف التاء تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects as manifest unbelief the claim that a saint outranks a prophet; al-Khidr was a prophet, and even otherwise Moses’ learning was a test and seeking more knowledge is commendable.
rows.anchor: وقد زال اقدام أقوام من الضلال في تفضيل الولي على النبي وهو كفر جلي حيث قالوا أمر موسى بالتعلم من الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book claim this was another Moses, son of Manan rather than Imran; the author says a saint can only be such by believing in a prophet and cannot outrank him.
rows.anchor: على ان أهل الكتاب يقولون ان موسى هذا ليس موسى بن عمران انما هو موسى بن مانان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was right to seek knowledge because increasing knowledge is always sought.
rows.anchor: ولا غضاضة في طلب موسى العلم لان الزيادة في العلم مطلوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first act is phrased as al-Khidr’s own wish because it outwardly looked corrupt; the last as God’s wish because it was pure grace beyond human power; the middle combines harm in action with benefit in replacement.
rows.anchor: وانما ذكر اولا فاردت لانه فساد في الظاهر وهو فعله وثالثا فأراد ربك لأنه أنعام محض وغير مقدور البشر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains fa-aradnā as meaning God wanted it; the Quran has many similar expressions.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج معنى فاردنا فاراد الله عز وجل ومثله في القرآن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners about Dhul-Qarnayn may have been Jews testing Muhammad or Abu Jahl and his associates.
rows.anchor: أي اليهود على جهة الامتحان أو أبو جهل واشياعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One identification is Alexander, ruler of the world; one report says the two believing world-rulers were Dhul-Qarnayn and Solomon, the disbelieving rulers Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar, and Dhul-Qarnayn came after Nimrod.
rows.anchor: هو الاسكندر الذي ملك الدنيا قيل ملكها مؤمنان ذو القرنين وسليمان وكافران نمرود وبختنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view calls him a righteous servant made king over the earth and granted knowledge and wisdom, with light guiding his way and darkness surrounding him from behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان عبدا صالحا ملكه الله الأرض وأعطاه العلم والحكمة وسخر له النور والظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views call him a prophet or an angelic king.
rows.anchor: وقيل نبيا وقيل ملكا من الملائكة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says he was neither king nor prophet but a righteous servant; God struck his right horn in obedience, he died and was raised, then struck the left horn and died again and was raised, hence the name.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه انه قال ليس بملك ولا نبي ولكن كان عبد صالحا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In the report, Ali says there is someone like Dhul-Qarnayn among the audience, meaning himself.
rows.anchor: وفيكم مثله أراد نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says people killed him when he called them to monotheism, and God brought him back to life.
rows.anchor: قيل كان يدعوهم إلى التوحيد فيقتلونه فيحييه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says he toured both horns, the eastern and western ends, of the world.
rows.anchor: الدنيا يعني جانبيها شرقها وغربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations derive the name from two braids, two generations passing in his lifetime, ruling Romans and Persians or Turks and Romans, or having two hornlike features on his crown or head.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان له قرنان أي ضفيرتان أو انقرض في وقته قرنان من الناس أو لأنه ملك الروم وفارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name is also explained by his noble lineage on both parents’ sides or by being Roman.
rows.anchor: أو كان كريم الطرفين أبا وأما وكان من الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase minhu refers to Dhul-Qarnayn: God will recount something about him.
rows.anchor: من ذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established Dhul-Qarnayn in the earth by giving him power and a high position there.
rows.anchor: جعلنا له فيها مكان واعتلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The means God gave him reached everything he wanted among the purposes and goals of his rule.
rows.anchor: أراده من اغراضه ومقاصده في ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sabab is a means, such as knowledge or power, by which one reaches an objective; Dhul-Qarnayn used successive means to reach west, east, and the two barriers.
rows.anchor: والسبب ما يتوصل به إلى المقصود من علم أو قدرة

rows.speaker: كوفي وشامي
rows.claim: Kufans and Shamis read attabaʿa with initial hamza and doubled tāʾ.
rows.anchor: ثم اتبع كوفي وشامي الباقون بوصل الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī distinguishes the forms: attabaʿa means to catch up, while ittabaʿa means to follow even without catching up.
rows.anchor: عن الاصمعي اتبع لحق واتبع اقتفى وان لم يلحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The setting of the sun means the western limit of inhabited land; the rising place is understood similarly.
rows.anchor: أي منتهى العمارة نحو المغرب وكذا المطلع

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says Dhul-Qarnayn found in books that a descendant of Shem would drink from the spring of life and live forever; he searched for it, with al-Khidr as his minister and cousin, and al-Khidr drank but Dhul-Qarnayn did not find it.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم بدء أمره أنه وجد في الكتب ان أحد أولاد سام يشرب من عين الحياة

rows.speaker: شامي وكوفي غير حفص
rows.claim: The Shami and Kufan readers except Hafs read ḥāmiyah, meaning hot, where the other reading is ḥamʾah, muddy.
rows.anchor: حامية شامي وكوفي غير حفص بمعنى حارة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet asked where the sun sets; Abu Dharr deferred to God and the Messenger, and the Prophet said it sets in a muddy spring.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ذر كنت رديف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على جمل فرأى الشمس حين غابت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Muawiya read ḥāmiyah, Ibn Abbas corrected him to ḥamʾah; Ibn Umar then read as the Commander of the Faithful had.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عند معاوية فقرأ معاوية حامية فقال ابن عباس حمئة

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar said the Torah likewise describes the sun setting in water and mud, agreeing with Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: ثم وجه إلى كعب الاحبار كيف تجد الشمس تغرب قال في ماء وطين كذلك نجد في التوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings do not conflict: the spring can be both muddy and hot.
rows.anchor: فوافق قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ولا تنافي فجازان تكون العين جامعة للوصفين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people near the spring were naked, wore animal skins, ate what the sea cast up, and were unbelievers.
rows.anchor: عراة من الثياب لباسهم جلود الصيد وطعامهم ما لفظ البحر وكانوا كفارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet, God revealed the choice to him; otherwise it was revealed to a prophet who instructed him, or it came by inspiration.
rows.anchor: ان كان نبيا فقد أوحى الله اليه بهذا والا فقد أوحى إلى نبي فامره النبي به أو كان الهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment could mean killing those who persisted in wrongdoing; beneficent treatment could mean honoring and teaching law to those who believed, or taking them captive, which is benevolent only relative to killing.
rows.anchor: خير بين ان يعذبهم بالقتل ان اصروا على أمرهم وبين ان يتخذ فيهم حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer is someone invited to Islam who persists in the grave wrong of associating partners with God; Dhul-Qarnayn kills him, and he then faces God’s severe punishment in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني أما من دعوته إلى الإسلام فابي الا البقاء على الظلم العظيم وهو الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment Dhul-Qarnayn imposes on earth is killing.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أما من ظلم فسوف نعذبه ﴾ بالقتل ﴿ ثم يرد إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer who acts as faith requires receives the reward of the best deed, identified as the testimony of faith.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأما من آمن وعمل صالحا ﴾ أي عمل ما يقتضيه الإيمان

rows.speaker: كوفي غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: Kufans except Abu Bakr read the construction as the best deed itself being the reward.
rows.anchor: جزاء الحسنى كوفي غير أبي بكر أي فله الفعلة الحسنى جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruler promises easy and accessible terms, without imposing difficult burdens such as onerous taxes or levies.
rows.anchor: أي ذا يسر أي لا نأمره بالصعب الشاق ولكن بالسهل المتيسر من الزكاة والخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people at the sun’s rising place were the Zanj.
rows.anchor: وهم الزنج

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says they had no buildings because the ground would not hold them, but underground passages; at sunrise they entered these and came out to work once the day rose.
rows.anchor: عن كعب ارضهم لا تمسك الأبنية وبها أسراب فإذا طلعت الشمس دخلوها فإذا ارتفع النهار خرجوا إلى معايشهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the missing screen as clothing: among Sudanese peoples, more people at the sunrise region went without clothes than anywhere else.
rows.anchor: أو الستر اللباس عن مجاهد من لا يلبس الثياب من السودان عند مطلع الشمس أكثر من جميع أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise may refer to Dhul-Qarnayn’s condition as described, magnifying his importance.
rows.anchor: أي أمر ذي القرنين كذلك أي كما وصفناه تعظيما لأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully knew all that Dhul-Qarnayn possessed, including troops, equipment, and the means of rule; khibr is a verbal-noun object because the verb contains the sense of being informed.
rows.anchor: نصب على المصدر لأن في أحطنا معنى خبرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he reached the sun’s rising place just as he reached its setting place, or the rising people resembled the western people as unbelievers subject to the same treatment of believers and persistent unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أو بلغ مطلع الشمس مثل ذلك أي كما بلغ مغربها أو تطلع على قوم مثل ذلك القبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two barriers are two mountains; Dhul-Qarnayn built a barrier across the gap, in a place at the edge of Turk lands toward the east.
rows.anchor: بين الجبلين وهما جبلان سد ذو القرنين ما بينهما

rows.speaker: مكي وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: Meccan, Abu Amr, and Hafs read the word for the barriers with fatḥa; Hamza and Ali use ḍamma, and the remaining readers use ḍamma on both forms.
rows.anchor: السدين وسدا مكي وأبو عمرو وحفص السدين وسدا حمزة وعلي وبضمهما غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation assigns ḍamma to natural barriers and fatḥa to barriers made by people.
rows.anchor: قيل ما كان مسدودا خلقة فهو مضموم وما كان من عمل العباد فهو مفتوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayna is a direct object of balagha, like an adverb that can be a noun; it is also genitive in firaqu bayni and nominative in taqaṭṭaʿa baynakum.
rows.anchor: وانتصب بين على انه مفعول به لبلغ كما أنجر بالاضافة في هذا فراق بيني وبينك وكما ارتفع في لقد تقطع بينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people living beyond the mountains were the Turks.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قوما ﴾ هم الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading means they understood speech only with great effort, using gestures and similar means.
rows.anchor: أي لا يكادون يفهمونه إلا بجهد ومشقة من اشارة ونحوها

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read the verb as meaning they could scarcely make their speech understood because their language was strange and unknown.
rows.anchor: يفقهون حمزة وعلى أي لا يفهمون السامع كلامهم ولا يبينونه لان لغتهم غريبة مجهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj are foreign names, as shown by their being diptote; only Asim pronounces their hamza.
rows.anchor: هما اسمانا أعجميان بدليل منع الصرف وهمزهما عاصم فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are said to descend from Japheth; another view says Yaʾjuj are Turks and Maʾjuj are the Jil and Daylam peoples.
rows.anchor: وهما من ولد يافث أو يأجوج من الترك ومأجوج من الجيل والديلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe them as man-eaters, or as raiders who in spring eat everything green and carry off what is dry; no one dies before seeing a thousand armed male descendants.
rows.anchor: قيل كانوا يأكلون الناس وقيل كانوا يخرجون أيام الربيع فلا يتركون شيئا اخضر إلا أكلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report divides them into two kinds, one excessively tall and the other excessively short.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم على صنفين طوال مفرطوا الطول وقصار مفرطوا القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharjan means tribute, a payment they would draw from their wealth; al-nul and al-nawal are comparable terms.
rows.anchor: خراجا حمزة وعلى أي جعلا نخرجه من أموالنا

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read the payment word as kharajan.
rows.anchor: خراجا حمزة وعلى أي جعلا

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The Meccan reading assimilates the doubled consonants in makkanī; another form leaves them distinct.
rows.anchor: بالادغام وبفكه مكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn says his Lord’s provision of wealth and power is better than their tribute, so he has no need of it.
rows.anchor: أي ما جعلني فيه مكينا من كثرة المال واليسار خير مما تبذلون لي من الخراج فلا حاجة لي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks them for skilled workers and craftsmen, together with the necessary tools.
rows.anchor: بفعلة وصناع يحسنون البناء والعمل وبالآلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A radm is a strong, secure wall or barrier, greater than a sadd.
rows.anchor: جدار أو حاجزا حصينا موثقا والردم اكبر من السد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubar are pieces of iron, and zubrah denotes a large piece.
rows.anchor: قطع الحديد والزبرة القطعة الكبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construction account says he dug the foundation to water, used rock and molten copper at the base, stacked iron with wood and charcoal between the mountains, then bellows heated it until molten copper fused with the iron into a solid mountain; the gap was reportedly one hundred farsakhs.
rows.anchor: قيل حفر الاساس حتى بلغ الماء وجعل الأساس من الصخر والنحاس المذاب والبنيان من زبر الحديد بينها الحطب والفحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ṣadafayn are the two sides of the mountains because they face one another.
rows.anchor: جانبي الجبلين لانهما يتصادقان أي يتقابلان

rows.speaker: مكي وبصري وشامي
rows.claim: Meccan, Basran, and Shami readers use the ṣadafayn form with the two vowels open.
rows.anchor: الصدفين مكي وبصري وشامي

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reads the alternate ṣudufayn form.
rows.anchor: الصدفين أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn tells the workers to blow the bellows into the iron.
rows.anchor: أي قال ذو القرنين للعملة انفخوا في الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the blown iron became like fire, he asked them to bring him molten copper and pour it over the iron.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال آتوني ﴾ اعطوني ﴿ أفرغ ﴾ اصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitran is molten copper because it drips; grammatically it is the object of afrighu, with the first object of ātūnī omitted because qitran follows.
rows.anchor: نحاسا مذابا لأنه يقطر وهو منصوب بافرغ وتقديره آتوني قطرا افرغ عليه قطرا

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza connects the imperative ātūnī with a connecting alif but starts it with a kasra, giving the sense bring it to me.
rows.anchor: قال ائتوني بوصل الألف حمزة وإذا ابتدأ كسر الألف أي جيئوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shorter form istaṭāʿū drops tāʾ for ease because tāʾ and ṭāʾ have nearby articulation points.
rows.anchor: بحذف التاء للخفة لأن التاء قريبة المخرج من الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could neither climb over the wall because of its height nor tunnel through it because it was solid.
rows.anchor: أي لا حيلة لهم فيه من صعود لارتفاعه ولا نقب لصلابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier is a mercy from God to His servants, or the providential capacity and power to build it.
rows.anchor: أي هذا السد نعمة من الله ورحمة على عباده أو هذا الاقدار والتمكين من تسويته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s promise refers to the coming of the Resurrection, whose approach is near.
rows.anchor: فإذا دنى مجئ يوم القيامة وشارف أن يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakkā means flattened and spread level with the ground; whatever is leveled after rising has been crushed flat.
rows.anchor: أي مدكوكا مبسوطا مسوى بالأرض وكل ما انبسط بعد ارتفاع فقد اندك

rows.speaker: كوفي
rows.claim: Kufans read dakkāʾ to mean level ground.
rows.anchor: دكاء كوفي أي أرضا مستوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God’s promise is true is the end of Dhul-Qarnayn’s speech.
rows.anchor: آخر قول ذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraknā means jaʿalnā, We made or left.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتركنا ﴾ وجعلنا ﴿ بعضهم ﴾ بعض الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones mixing together may be all created beings, confused and intermingled, humans and jinn; alternatively, they are Gog and Magog, surging into the lands when they emerge from behind the barrier.
rows.anchor: أي يضطربون ويختلطون انسهم وجنهم حيارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gog and Magog drink the sea, eat its creatures, trees, and people they encounter, cannot reach Mecca, Medina, or Jerusalem, then God sends larvae into their necks and ears and they die.
rows.anchor: وروى انهم يأتون البحر فيشربون ماءه ويأكلون دوابه ثم يأكلون الشجر ومن ظفروا به من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is blown for the Hour, and all creatures are gathered for reward and punishment; jamʿan emphatically confirms the gathering.
rows.anchor: والعقاب ﴿ جمعا ﴾ تأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displays Hell to the disbelievers so they see and witness it.
rows.anchor: وأظهرناها لهم فرأوها وشاهدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The veil over their eyes may be from God’s signs, which they look at, or from the Quran, which they should honor and remember, or from reading and pondering its meanings.
rows.anchor: عن آياتي التي ينظر إليها أو عن القرآن فأذكره بالتعظيم أو عن القرآن وتأمل معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to hear means they are deaf to revelation; this wording is stronger than ordinary deafness, since a deaf person may hear when shouted at, while these people are as if made entirely deaf.
rows.anchor: أي كانوا صما عنه إلا انه ابلغ إذ الاصم قد يستطيع السمع إذا صيح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers wrongly think that taking angels or Jesus as protectors apart from God will benefit them; this is an evil assumption.
rows.anchor: يعني الملائكة وعيسى عليهم السلام أولياء نافعهم بئس ما ظنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the syntax in which anna and its clause fill both objects of afahasiba, while ʿibādī and awliyāʾ are the objects of ittakhadhū; the sense is that these are not their protectors.
rows.anchor: وقيل ان بصلتها سد مسد مفعولي أفحسب وعبادي أولياء مفعولا أن يتخذوا وهذا أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzulan is what is prepared for a guest’s arrival, such as a lodging; the verse threatens the disbelievers with painful punishment.
rows.anchor: هو ما يقام للتنزيل وهو الضيف ونحوه فبشرهم بعذاب اليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam explains their recompense by apposition, and is their punishment because they disbelieved and mocked God’s signs and messengers.
rows.anchor: أي جزاؤهم جهنم بكفرهم واستهزائهم بآيات الله ورسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalidīna is a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ﴿ خالدين فيها ﴾ حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not desiring a change may mean they are content with their gift and do not want a better place; it may be the ultimate description, since people in worldly bliss still yearn for something higher; or it may simply deny any transition and confirm eternity.
rows.anchor: بما أعطوا يقال حال من مكانه حولا أي لا مزيد عليها حتى تنازعهم أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea means seawater, and by extension the whole sea as a kind.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قل لو كان البحر ﴾ أي ماء البحر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda defines midād as the material used for writing.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة المداد ما يكتب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the sea were writing ink for recording God’s knowledge and wisdom, it would run out before His words; another sea of equal size would also run out, while the words do not.
rows.anchor: أي لو كتبت كلمات علم الله وحكمته وكان البحر مدادا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mithlahu means another sea like it; madadan is a specification or tamyīz, and the word refers to material that replenishes ink.
rows.anchor: لنفذ أيضا والكلمات غير نافذة مددا تمييز نحو لي مثله رجلا

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى
rows.claim: Hamza and Ali read the form of the verb for being exhausted with a voiced dhāl.
rows.anchor: ينفذ حمزة وعلى

rows.speaker: حيي بن أخطب
rows.claim: Huyayy ibn Akhtab challenged the Quran’s claim of abundant wisdom against its statement that people received only a little knowledge; the passage was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: قيل قال حيي بن أخطب في كتابكم ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا ثم تقرءون وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response means that the knowledge given is indeed much, yet only a drop from the sea of God’s words.
rows.anchor: يعني أن ذلك خير كثير ولكنه قطرة من بحر كلمات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is a human like his audience, distinguished by receiving revelation that their God is one God.
rows.anchor: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yarjū liqāʾa rabbihi may mean hoping for a gracious, accepted meeting with God or fearing an evil meeting; liqāʾ can mean coming before God, or—its literal sense—seeing Him, in which case hope remains literal.
rows.anchor: فمن كان يأمل حسن لقاء ربه وأن يلقاه لقاء رضا وقبول أو فمن كان يخاف سوء لقاء ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous act is sincere, done only for God’s sake without mixing in another motive.
rows.anchor: خالصا لا يريد به إلا وجه ربه ولا يخلط به غيره

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh defines a righteous act as one a person would not be ashamed of.
rows.anchor: وعن يحيى بن معاذ هو مالا يستحي منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition can target associating partners with God or ostentation; the Prophet calls ostentation the lesser shirk in response to a question.
rows.anchor: هو نهي عن الشرك أو عن الرياء قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا الشرك الاصغر قالوا وما الشرك الأصغر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies the lesser shirk as ostentation.
rows.anchor: قال الرياء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report promises protection from every trial for eight days to anyone who recites Sūrat al-Kahf, including protection from the Antichrist if he appears then.
rows.anchor: عليه وسلم من قرأ سورة الكهف فهو معصوم ثمانية أيام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report says reciting the verse before sleep creates a light to Mecca filled with angels praying for the reciter until waking; from Mecca the light reaches the Frequented House.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي إلى آخرها عند مضجعه كان له نورا يتلألأ

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the disjoint letters are God’s greatest name.
rows.anchor: قال السدي هو اسم الله الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the letters are the name of the surah.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اسم للسورة

rows.speaker: علي ويحيى
rows.claim: Ali and Yahya read the hāʾ and yāʾ with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ على ويحيى بكسر الهاء والياء

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi reads both vowels between fatḥa and kasra, closer to fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ونافع بين الفتح والكسر وإلى الفتح أقرب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads hāʾ with kasra and yāʾ with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وأبو عمرو بكسر الهاء وفتح الياء

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza uses the reverse, hāʾ with fatḥa and yāʾ with kasra.
rows.anchor: وحمزة بعكسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on both letters.
rows.anchor: وغيرهم بفتحهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikru raḥmati rabbika is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this is a mention of your Lord’s mercy.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ أي هذا ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbdahu is the direct object of raḥmah.
rows.anchor: مفعول الرحمة

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلي وحفص
rows.claim: Hamza, Ali, and Hafs read Zakariyya with a shortened final vowel, and take it as an apposition to ʿabdahu.
rows.anchor: بالقصر حمزة وعلي وحفص وهو بدل من عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is an adverb attached to raḥmah.
rows.anchor: ظرف للرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret prayer follows the command and avoids ostentation, drawing the worshipper nearer to purity.
rows.anchor: دعاه دعاء سرا كما هو المأمور به وهو أبعد عن الرياء وأقرب إلى الصفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Zechariah hid his prayer so he would not be blamed for asking for a child in old age; he was seventy-five or eighty.
rows.anchor: أو أخفاه لئلا يلام على طلب الولد في أوان الكبر لأنه كان ابن خمس وسبعين أو ثمانين سنة
